_meta.description: Credential card registry. The single INDEX of credentials this install uses. Metadata only, never a value.
_meta.location_rationale: Lives OUTSIDE every credential store on purpose. The denylist hook matches the bare store name at any depth, so a registry stored inside one would be unreadable by the agent, defeating the point of cards.
_meta.how_to_use: python3 scripts/cred.py list | show <id> | check <id> | exec <id> --as VAR -- cmd | keys <id> | intake <id> | verified <id> | audit. Procedure: Nate's-kb/security-protocol.md section 2.

_rules.ABSOLUTE: A card NEVER contains a credential value. Not a key, not a token, not a password, not a fragment.
_rules.what_a_card_holds: What the credential is, which file holds it, the key NAME, which script resolves it, scope, sensitivity, rotation and expiry, and when it was last proven alive by a real call.
_rules.key_names_vs_values: Key names are not secrets. Values are.
_rules.filenames_can_carry_identifiers: Enumerating a store is allowed, but some credential filenames embed an identifier (Google OAuth downloads put the client ID in the filename; AWS key CSVs and cert files do similar). Low sensitivity, but it does enter the transcript.
_rules.why: Two things sound identical and are not: (A) a script resolving a credential at runtime so the value never enters agent context; and (B) the agent reading a value into context, which the denylist exists to prevent. Values in agent context propagate to session logs, [CAPTURE:] markers headed for the KB stores, compaction summaries and shell history.
_rules.reading_key_names_safely: Never pipe credential lines through a transform that assumes KEY=value: a bare-value line has no '=', so a masking transform prints it whole. Enumerate by filename, and match only positively-identified [A-Z_]+ tokens (cred.py keys does this).
_rules.health_is_proven_only_by_a_live_call: A local status check (token age, file present) does not reflect server-side revocation. Only a live list/read call is authoritative, so last_verified_live is the only health field that means anything.

_schema.store: repo-relative .secrets store, or an out-of-repo path
_schema.path: full path to the file holding the value
_schema.key_name: the variable/key NAME, or null if not yet confirmed. NEVER the value.
_schema.resolution: how a script extracts the value at runtime
_schema.sensitivity: admin | service | payment | personal | recovery | unknown
_schema.used_by: list of scripts/systems that resolve this at runtime, or [] if none known
_schema.scope: what the credential is permitted to do
_schema.health_check: the live call that would prove this credential works, or null if none defined
_schema.last_verified_live: YYYY-MM-DD of the last successful real call, or null if never
_schema.grounded: what was actually verified this session, vs inherited from a KB entry
_schema.resolver: machine-readable resolution: {type: env|fernet-json|file|aws-profile|external|manual, file, key, key_file, field, profile, how, site, covers[]}. See the scripts/cred.py docstring.

_example_card.what: Example: API key for a weather service used by a daily-report script
_example_card.notes: Illustration only. It sits outside `cards`, so cred.py ignores it. Copy its shape for your first real card.

_pending_cards.description: Credential files confirmed present but not yet carded because scope, owner or consumer is unconfirmed. Carding them without grounding would manufacture false metadata.

_audit.description: Inputs for scripts/cred.py audit (run by scripts/maintenance.py). stores = credential stores whose every file must be carded, pending, or ignored. ignore = files that are deliberately not credentials, each with its reason in ignore_reasons. consumer_dirs = where to look for scripts that name a carded file by path instead of by card id.
